entry.title: Taking the Bite Out of Mosquito-Borne Disease

media:group.media:title: Taking the Bite Out of Mosquito-Borne Disease
media:group.media:description:
Mosquitoes are the deadliest animals on Earth, but new science could change that. At UC San Diego, researchers are engineering mosquitoes to help bring us closer to a world free from mosquito-borne diseases like malaria and dengue.
This work represents a new approach to prevention, protecting people, reducing strain on health systems and moving us toward a future where mosquito-borne disease no longer threatens lives.
Learn more about how UC San Diego’s research impacts your life at: @aking-the-bite-out-of-mosquito-borne-disease/

entry.title: The Right Cancer Care, Right Now

media:group.media:title: The Right Cancer Care, Right Now
media:group.media:description:
What if cancer patients didn’t have to wait weeks for answers? At UC San Diego, researchers are developing AI-powered tools that rapidly analyze biopsies — helping doctors identify the best treatment options faster, more accurately and at lower cost.
By reducing delays between diagnosis and care, these tools have the potential to save lives, ease uncertainty for patients and expand access to precision cancer treatment.
Learn more about how UC San Diego’s research impacts your life at: @he-right-cancer-care-right-now/

entry.title: Revolutionizing Preventative Healthcare With Just A Touch

media:group.media:title: Revolutionizing Preventative Healthcare With Just A Touch
media:group.media:description:
UC San Diego engineers and medical researchers are creating wearable sensors that continuously track health markers like blood pressure, glucose, fatigue and hydration. These sensors turn everyday movement into actionable data, helping doctors detect issues earlier and deliver more personalized care.
By monitoring multiple biomarkers at once, this technology makes it easier to manage medical conditions and optimize health seamlessly and in real time.
Learn more about how UC San Diego’s research impacts your life at: @evolutionizing-preventative-healthcare-with-just-a-touch/

entry.title: The Best Lab is Real Life

media:group.media:title: The Best Lab is Real Life
media:group.media:description:
The Living Lab brings UC San Diego researchers and older adults together to explore what supports strength, independence and connection as people age. From fall prevention to brain health, residents help turn research into practical tools that enhance everyday care.
By meeting people where they are, the Living Lab lowers barriers to participation and transforms aging research into solutions that improve lives today and for generations to come.
Learn more about how UC San Diego’s research impacts your life at: @he-best-lab-is-real-life/

entry.title: Harnessing the Power of Human Milk

media:group.media:title: Harnessing the Power of Human Milk
media:group.media:description:
Human milk is universal, and its health benefits extend far beyond infancy. At UC San Diego’s Human Milk Institute, researchers are uncovering how human milk supports immune health, development and healing across the lifespan.
As the world’s first research institute dedicated solely to human milk, HMI brings together scientists, clinicians, engineers and community partners to turn discovery into better care and equitable access. From infant health to chronic disease research, this work is expanding what’s possible and who benefits.
Learn more about how UC San Diego’s research impacts your life at: @arnessing-the-power-of-human-milk/

media:group.media:title: Cleaner Air. Safer Communities.
media:group.media:description:
UC San Diego researchers have uncovered a direct airborne link between contaminated waterways and the air surrounding nearby communities. By studying how pollutants aerosolize and move through the atmosphere, scientists are identifying new public health risks and developing tools to monitor exposure and inform policy.
This research is helping protect communities today while shaping cleaner, safer environments for the future.
Learn more about how UC San Diego’s research impacts your life at: @leaner-air-safer-communities/

media:group.media:title: Staying Ahead of Natural Disasters
media:group.media:description:
Led by UC San Diego, ALERTCalifornia is a statewide network of more than 1,200 cameras and sensors providing real-time wildfire intelligence to emergency managers. The system helps spot wildfire smoke, monitor active fires, scale response efforts and inform evacuations.
To manage the massive volume of data, ALERTCalifornia uses artificial intelligence to support early wildfire detection. This award-winning public safety program turns real-time data into action — helping communities prepare for, respond to and recover from natural disasters.
Learn more about how UC San Diego’s research impacts your life at: @taying-ahead-of-natural-disasters/

media:group.media:title: Moving Performance Forward
media:group.media:description:
How we move shapes how we live. At UC San Diego’s Human Performance Institute, researchers study the science of movement, recovery and resilience, translating performance science into tools that help people move better, recover faster and live healthier lives.
From elite athletes to everyday movement, this interdisciplinary work blends medicine, engineering, and biomechanics to turn research into real-world impact.
Learn more about how UC San Diego’s research impacts your life at : @oving-performance-forward/

entry.title: Flesh-Eating Screwworms Have Returned. Can New Technology Stop Them?

media:group.media:title: Flesh-Eating Screwworms Have Returned. Can New Technology Stop Them?
media:group.media:description:
A version of this video with audio description track is available here: https://youtu.be/TwhM6zYHons
New World screwworm flies, highly destructive parasitic insects, have returned to parts of the U.S. and pose a significant danger. Professor Omar Akbari of the Department of Cell and Developmental Biology discusses how the insect was eliminated in the past and the ways new genetics technologies could help control today’s threat.

entry.title: Jeremy’s Story: Research at UC San Diego Offers Hope for Rare Disease (Extended Audio Description)

media:group.media:title: Jeremy’s Story: Research at UC San Diego Offers Hope for Rare Disease (Extended Audio Description)
media:group.media:description: Uri Manor, inaugural faculty director of the Goeddel Family Technology Sandbox, is using the center’s advanced instruments to study Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, a debilitating genetic neurological disorder. These advancements are offering hope for six-year-old Jeremy, his parents and others who suffer from the disease.
